diagnostics.message: :data.aws_ecs_task_definition.this: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_ecs_task_definition.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

The explicit `depends_on = [aws_ecs_task_definition.this]` on data.aws_ecs_task_definition.this is redundant: the data source already reads `aws_ecs_task_definition.this[0].family` via its `task_definition` argument, which creates the same implicit dependency and forces the same ordering.

aws_ecs_service.this should depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec. The service launches tasks whose containers are pulled and logged using the task execution role; the only implicit path (service -> task definition -> execution_role_arn -> aws_iam_role.task_exec) ensures the role exists but not that its policy is attached. Without waiting for the attachment, first-deployment task launches can fail with AccessDenied on ECR/CloudWatch Logs while the attachment is still propagating — the same race the module already guards against for the service role via `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service]`.

aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition should depend on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec for the same reason as aws_ecs_service.this: tasks launched by this service use the task execution role to pull images and emit logs, and the implicit dependency chain only covers the role itself, not the attachment of its policy. A bare `depends_on` mirrors the existing `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service]` already present on this resource.
